summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, chronic venous thromboembolism, interstitial lung disease, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and URI symptoms one week after a prior discharge. She had gained 10 pounds, attributed to poor adherence to a low-sodium diet, and was treated with intravenous diuretics. Her respiratory symptoms were determined to be from a viral upper respiratory infection, not pneumonia, and antibiotics were withheld. She improved with diuresis, losing 9 pounds, and was transitioned from furosemide to torsemide for better bioavailability. Iron therapy was started for iron deficiency anemia, and warfarin was held briefly for an elevated INR before being safely restarted. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, instructions to monitor daily weights, and follow-up plans with her PCP and specialists.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
